unit.why: A single narrative: R. Yosef Yampoler asks the Besht to take him to the Land of Israel, is refused, predicts the Besht's failure and his own arrival, and is carried there by a noblewoman's ship.

stories.start_quote: אביו של הה״ק ר׳ יצחק הנ״ל
stories.end_quote: והביאה אותו לאה״ק. ומנ״כ שם זי״ע
stories.summary_en: R. Yosef 'Spravedlivy' asks the Besht to take him along to the Holy Land; the Besht, fearing his strictness, puts him off; R. Yosef predicts that the Besht, travelling like royalty, will not arrive while he, travelling like a beggar, will; the Besht's ship breaks up, and a noblewoman sees R. Yosef studying on the shore and brings him to the Land of Israel, where he is buried.

tags.why: The Land of Israel is the destination around which the whole story turns.

quotes: אתם תסעו כמו מלכות ולא תבואו לשם
tags.why: His prediction about both journeys comes true.
The story's arc is a prediction that is fulfilled.

quotes: נסע הרה״ק ר״י הנ״ל אל הבעש״ט לבקש ממנו
tags.why: One tzaddik travels to another tzaddik, the Besht, with a request.

quotes: הבעש״ט נסע ונשבר הספינה והוכרח לשוב לביתו
tags.why: The Besht's failed journey to the Holy Land.

quotes: הבעש״ט הי' ירא מעונש הקפדה שלו
tags.why: The Besht fears the punishment R. Yosef's strictness might bring.
A noblewoman, apparently a non-Jew, carries him on her ship.
The noblewoman acts in a small but decisive role.

quotes: ישב על שפת הים וספר בידו ולמד שם
tags.why: He is studying on the shore when he is found.

quotes: אתם תסעו כמו מלכות ולא תבואו לשם ואני נוסע לשם כמו בעטלער
tags.why: Implicit rivalry with the Besht over who will reach the Land.
Travelling humbly like a beggar, set against royal travel.

quotes: וראתה מרחוק איש יושב על שפת הים
tags.why: Providential rescue that is not explicitly called a miracle.
Only a closing note that he is buried in the Holy Land.
